name: Map My CORE subject guide for Kai
status: Approved by The ME Project for upload on 17 November 2026. Each entry carries its own status; follow rule_for_kai for entries marked not yet researched, not confirmed or not yet official. Recheck at least yearly and after any announced change.
rule_for_kai: Use only this guide for anything about school subjects, streams, tracks or sections. Never add from your own knowledge.
First ask the student's country, school system and grade.
Say 'students interested in this field usually take...' and 'for example, [university] asked for ... in [year]'. Never say 'you should', 'you need' or 'you must'.
Always add that requirements differ between universities and change, and that the school counsellor and the university's official website have the final word.

Never discourage a curiosity because of subjects already chosen. If a usual subject is missing, say that routes often exist (foundation, bridging or qualifying programmes, or a track change where the system allows it) and suggest asking the counsellor.
If an entry is missing or marked 'not yet researched', 'not confirmed' or 'not yet official', say you do not have checked information and point to the counsellor.
Quote the year of any example or rule you mention.

UAE.note: No national admission rule since November 2024; each university sets its own. Ministry stream decision at end of grade 8/9; moving into the Advanced stream is not possible in grades 11-12.

MED.usual_pattern: Biology and chemistry, plus maths or physics, at high grades. In the Ministry system: the Advanced or Elite stream.
MED.examples:
UAE University (Jan 2025): 90% in maths and 90% in two of biology, chemistry, physics (or A-level B, IB 5, AP 4), plus an entry test and interviews. General and Applied stream students, and Indian and Pakistani board students, are not admitted to medicine.
University of Sharjah (2023–24): biology and chemistry required. British: both at IGCSE plus B at AS or C at A-level in one. IB: both studied, 5 at HL in one. American: two biology, two chemistry and one physics course at B or above.
Ajman University (June 2026): medicine asks for 85% (Elite) or 90% (Advanced) with 90% in maths and in two of biology, chemistry, physics; the General stream is not listed. British: chemistry, biology, physics, maths and English at IGCSE (four A, one B) plus two sciences at AS or A-level. IB: two sciences at HL, 32 points. Indian boards: 85% with physics, chemistry and biology in grade 12 at 80%.
University of Sharjah (FAQ, 2025–26): the General stream is not accepted for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy or physiotherapy.
Veterinary medicine at UAE University: ranked by maths and science, plus interviews.

PHARM.usual_pattern: Biology and chemistry, usually with maths. Dentistry and pharmacy are admitted like medicine at most UAE universities, at a slightly lower grade.
PHARM.examples:
Ajman University (June 2026): dentistry 80% (Elite) or 85% (Advanced) with 90% in maths and two sciences; pharmacy 70% or 75% with 80% in maths and two sciences; the General stream is not listed for either.
University of Sharjah (2023–24 and 2025–26 FAQ): dentistry and pharmacy require biology and chemistry; General stream not accepted.
Higher Colleges of Technology (2025): medical laboratory science is an applied bachelor open to the Advanced (70%) and General (80%) streams, with physics and chemistry or biology required for science-based programmes.
UK pattern (Russell Group): biomedical sciences and biochemistry: chemistry and biology.

ALLIED.usual_pattern: Biology is the usual base; chemistry commonly expected.
ALLIED.examples:
UAE University (Jan 2025): nutrition, dietetics and speech-language pathology have no fixed minimum; applicants are ranked by maths and science grades when places are short.
University of Sharjah (2023–24): health sciences accept the General stream only through a qualifying programme covering chemistry, biology, physics and maths.
Ajman University (June 2026): nursing 60% (Elite), 65% (Advanced) or 70% (General), English 80%; physiotherapy 60%, 70% or 75%, English 80%.
Higher Colleges of Technology (2025): nursing, midwifery, emergency medical services and health information management are applied bachelors open to the Advanced and General streams.
University of Sharjah (FAQ, 2025–26): General stream not accepted for physiotherapy; accepted for other health sciences with a preparatory semester.
UK pattern (Russell Group): nursing usually asks for biology; physiotherapy biology, sometimes a second science.

ENG.usual_pattern: Maths and physics. Chemistry as well for chemical, petroleum and materials engineering.
ENG.examples:
UAE University (Jan 2025): 80% in maths, 80% in physics and in chemistry or biology (or A-level C, IB 4, AP 3).
Khalifa University (2025–26): maths and two sciences in grade 12; 80% from the Advanced or Elite stream, 90% from the General stream; British: three AS or A-levels including maths and one science at C; IB: maths and one science, 4 in each; CBSE: maths and two sciences, 75%. Its own test covers maths, physics and chemistry.
American University of Sharjah: B or above in maths and physics for science and engineering majors.
Zayed University (2025): intelligent systems engineering asks for 85% in maths, 80% in physics and 80% in another science; British: two A-levels at C in related subjects; IB: two related HL subjects at 5.
Ajman University (June 2026): engineering 75% (Elite), 80% (Advanced) or 90% (General), with 80% in maths and physics and 80% in biology or chemistry.
American University in Dubai (2025–26): maths, physics and one science; 75%, 80% or 90% by stream.
Emirates Aviation University (2024–25): aeronautical and aerospace engineering and aircraft maintenance: 70% (Elite), 75% (Advanced) or 80% (General) in maths and physics; British: maths and physics at AS level.
University of Sharjah (FAQ, 2025–26): General stream admitted to engineering with a placement test in physics and maths.
UK pattern: chemical engineering: chemistry and maths.

COMP.usual_pattern: Maths. One science is often expected; physics is useful.
COMP.examples:
Khalifa University (2025–26): computer science asks for maths and one of physics, chemistry or biology.
University of Sharjah (2023–24): computer engineering and cybersecurity need the scientific route with two sciences and maths.
Higher Colleges of Technology (2025): data science, cybersecurity and software engineering are applied bachelors open to the Advanced (70%) and General (80%) streams.
UK pattern (Russell Group): computing: computing, maths and physics useful.

INFOSYS.usual_pattern: Maths helps. No particular subjects at most universities.
INFOSYS.examples:
UAE University (Jan 2025): information technology has no fixed minimum; ranked by maths and science.
University of Sharjah (2023–24): information systems and multimedia technology set a minimum average only, with no named subjects.
Ajman University (June 2026): IT networking and security 60%, 70% or 75% by stream with 75% in maths; information systems project management with 70% in maths.

LIFESCI.usual_pattern: Biology and chemistry; maths useful. Two of biology, chemistry and geography for environmental science.
LIFESCI.examples:
Khalifa University (2025–26): cell and molecular biology asks for maths and one of physics, chemistry or biology.
UAE University (Jan 2025): science and agriculture have no fixed minimum; ranked by maths and science.
American University in Dubai (2025–26): biology asks for 70% in one science.
UK pattern (Russell Group): biology: biology and chemistry; environmental science: two of biology, chemistry, geography.

PHYSMATH.usual_pattern: Maths for all. Physics for physics; chemistry for chemistry; two sciences for geology.
PHYSMATH.examples:
Khalifa University (2025–26): maths and science for all science programmes; chemistry for the chemistry degree; maths and one science for applied maths, statistics and data science.
UK pattern (Russell Group): physics: maths and physics; mathematics and actuarial routes: maths, further maths useful; geology: two of maths, physics, chemistry, biology.

ECONFIN.usual_pattern: Maths is usually expected. Economics and business as school subjects are useful where offered.
ECONFIN.examples:
UAE University (Jan 2025): business and economics have no fixed minimum; ranked by maths grade when places are short.
UK pattern (Russell Group): economics: maths essential; accountancy: maths essential, business and economics useful.
ECONFIN.status: Partly sourced. UAE examples naming maths for economics or finance: to add.

BUSMGMT.usual_pattern: No particular subjects are usually required. Maths helps.
BUSMGMT.examples:
UAE University (Jan 2025): business has no fixed minimum; ranked by maths grade when places are short.
University of Sharjah (2023–24): business administration sets a minimum average only.
American University of Sharjah: B or above in specified subjects for business majors (subjects not listed on the page read).
Ajman University (June 2026): management, marketing, finance, accounting and hospitality management: 60% in every stream, English 80%, no named subjects.
Higher Colleges of Technology (2025): business analytics, marketing, accounting, finance, tourism, logistics and HR open to the Advanced and General streams.
Emirates Aviation University (2024–25): aviation management 70% overall, no maths or physics requirement.
UK pattern (Russell Group): business and management: none essential; maths, business and economics useful.

LAW.usual_pattern: No particular subjects. Strong Arabic for law taught in Arabic; strong English and essay subjects for law taught in English.
LAW.examples:
UAE University (Jan 2025): law asks for 70% in maths and 80% in Arabic.
University of Sharjah (2023–24): law sets a minimum average only.
Ajman University (June 2026): law 60% in every stream with 70% in maths.
University of Dubai (2024–25, law with a University of London route): 70% (Elite), 75% (Advanced) or 80% (General); British: five IGCSE plus two AS or one A-level; IB 80%; Indian 65%; a maths placement score.
UK pattern (Russell Group): law: English; history and other essay subjects useful.

SOC.usual_pattern: No particular subjects for most. One science is useful for psychology. Essay subjects (history, English, Arabic) are useful for politics and policy.
SOC.examples:
UAE University (Jan 2025): humanities and social sciences have no fixed minimum; ranked by maths.
University of Sharjah (2023–24): arts, social sciences and humanities set a minimum average only.
Ajman University (June 2026): psychology, sociology and social work: 60% in every stream, no named subjects.
UK pattern (Russell Group): psychology: one of biology, chemistry or physics; sociology and politics: none essential.

EDU.usual_pattern: No particular subjects for primary and early years. For secondary teaching: the subject you would teach.
EDU.examples:
UAE University (Jan 2025): education has no fixed minimum; ranked by maths.
Higher Colleges of Technology (2025): early childhood education is an applied bachelor open to the Advanced and General streams.
UK pattern (Russell Group): secondary teacher training: at least one subject from the school curriculum you would teach.

ARCH.usual_pattern: Maths and often physics, plus art or design and a portfolio of work.
ARCH.examples:
American University of Sharjah: a portfolio for architecture and interior design, and B or above in specified subjects; STEM majors may need B in maths and physics.
Zayed University (2025): architecture asks for 80% in maths (or SAT 500).
Ajman University (June 2026): architecture 65%, 70% or 75% by stream, English 80%; architectural engineering as for engineering (maths, physics and a science at 80%); interior design 60% in every stream.
American University in Dubai (2025–26): architecture needs a portfolio (three artworks and three building photos with a written justification) and SAT maths 590 or a placement test.
UK pattern (Russell Group): architecture: art at many universities; maths, design and technology or physics useful; portfolio.

DESIGN.usual_pattern: Art or design and a portfolio of work. Maths or computing useful for interaction and game design.
DESIGN.examples:
American University of Sharjah: a portfolio for design management.
University of Sharjah (2023–24): fine arts and design set a minimum average only.
American University in Dubai (2025–26): visual communication and interior design: maths placement, no portfolio stated.
Higher Colleges of Technology (2025): design and media production, digital media: applied bachelors open to the Advanced and General streams.
UK pattern (Russell Group): art and design: art plus a portfolio; computer games design: ICT or computing, with maths, art and design useful.

MEDIA.usual_pattern: No particular subjects. English, Arabic or media studies are usual.
MEDIA.examples:
University of Sharjah (2023–24): communication sets a minimum average only, with no named subjects.
Ajman University (June 2026): mass communication 60% in every stream, no named subjects.
University of Sharjah (FAQ, 2025–26): communication needs an interview; Arabic-track mass communication and public relations ask for an EmSAT-equivalent score.
UK pattern (Russell Group): media and communication: English or media studies.

ARTS.usual_pattern: Music usually needs music study, an instrument grade and an audition. Performing arts: an audition. Literature: the language. Archaeology: no particular subjects; history and a science useful.
ARTS.examples:
UAE examples: not yet researched.
UK pattern (Russell Group): music: music plus grade 7 or 8 on an instrument; English: English literature; archaeology: none essential.
ARTS.status: Not yet researched in the UAE.

SPORT.usual_pattern: One science (often biology) for sport and exercise science. No particular subjects for sports management and coaching.
SPORT.examples:
UAE University (Jan 2025): health and physical education sits in the College of Education: no fixed minimum, ranked by maths.
UK pattern (Russell Group): sports science: one of biology, chemistry, maths or physics; PE and psychology useful.

APPLIED.usual_pattern: These routes have their own entry rules (colleges, academies and licensing bodies), often including maths, physics, English and medical fitness.
APPLIED.examples:
Emirates Aviation University (2024–25): aircraft maintenance engineering: maths and physics (70%, 75% or 80% by stream); aviation management: 70% overall, no named subjects. No undergraduate pilot programme; pilot training is through flight academies with their own entry rules.
Higher Colleges of Technology (2025): aviation engineering and vocational diplomas (60% Advanced, 70% General).
Police and military colleges: not yet researched.

Saudi Arabia.note: Track chosen after the first secondary year. Weighted admission score at most universities: 30% school, 30% aptitude test, 40% achievement test. Scientific achievement test for General, Health and Life, Computer Science and Engineering tracks; theoretical for Sharia and Business.

MED.usual_pattern: Health and Life track is the natural route; the General and Computer Science and Engineering tracks are also accepted. Scientific Achievement Test. High averages.
MED.examples:
Imam University (1447/48, 2025–26): health and applied colleges accept the General, Health and Life, and Computer Science and Engineering tracks; medicine asks for a 90% average and at least 80 on the tests; weights 30/30/40.
King Saud University (1446): medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, emergency medical services, nursing and applied medical sciences accept only the General, Computer Science and Engineering, and Health and Life tracks; weights 30/30/40.
King Abdulaziz University (1447): health and science colleges accept the same three tracks.

PHARM.usual_pattern: As for medicine: Health and Life, General or Computer Science and Engineering track; scientific Achievement Test.
PHARM.examples: King Saud University (1446): pharmacy and applied medical sciences accept the three scientific tracks only.

ALLIED.usual_pattern: As for medicine. Nursing adds an interview at some universities.
ALLIED.examples:
King Saud University (1446): nursing and applied medical sciences accept the three scientific tracks only.
Imam University (1447/48): nursing requires a personal interview.

ENG.usual_pattern: Computer Science and Engineering track is the natural route; General and Health and Life also accepted. Scientific Achievement Test.
ENG.examples:
King Saud University (1446): engineering accepts only the General, Computer Science and Engineering, and Health and Life tracks.
KFUPM (2025): accepts the same three tracks and international-school science students; weighted score 50% aptitude, 40% achievement, 10% school average, or an early-admission test; SAT 1350 route.
King Abdulaziz University (1447): science colleges accept the same three tracks.

COMP.usual_pattern: Computer Science and Engineering track (cybersecurity is one of its subjects); General and Health and Life also accepted.
COMP.examples: King Saud University (1446): computer and information sciences accept the three scientific tracks only. KFUPM (2025): as for engineering.

INFOSYS.usual_pattern: Any scientific track; information systems programmes that sit in business colleges also accept the Business track.
INFOSYS.examples: King Saud University (1446): computer and information sciences: scientific tracks only; business administration college: scientific tracks plus the Business track.

LIFESCI.usual_pattern: Health and Life or General track; scientific Achievement Test.
LIFESCI.examples: King Saud University (1446): sciences, and food and agriculture, accept the three scientific tracks only. King Abdulaziz University (1447): same.

PHYSMATH.usual_pattern: Computer Science and Engineering or General track; scientific Achievement Test.
PHYSMATH.examples: King Saud University (1446): sciences college accepts the three scientific tracks only.

ECONFIN.usual_pattern: Business Administration track is the natural route (accounting, economics and finance are among its subjects); the three scientific tracks are also accepted.
ECONFIN.examples:
King Abdulaziz University (1447): the Faculty of Economics and Administration and the Rabigh business college accept the General, Computer Science and Engineering, Health and Life, and Business Administration tracks.
Imam University (1447/48): the Business Administration track leads to the College of Business.
King Saud University (1446): business administration accepts the three scientific tracks and the Business track; not the Sharia track.

BUSMGMT.usual_pattern: As for economics and finance: Business Administration track, or any scientific track.

LAW.usual_pattern: Sharia track is the natural route for sharia; law colleges also take the Business and scientific tracks at some universities. Theoretical Achievement Test for Sharia and Business tracks.
LAW.examples:
King Saud University (1446): law and political science sits among the humanities colleges, which accept all five tracks.
King Abdulaziz University (1447): humanities colleges accept all five tracks.

SOC.usual_pattern: Any track. Humanities colleges accept all five.
SOC.examples: King Saud University (1446): humanities and social sciences, and law and political science, accept all five tracks. King Abdulaziz University (1447): same.

EDU.usual_pattern: Any track for early childhood and humanities subjects; a scientific track for teaching science or maths.
EDU.examples: King Saud University (1446): education accepts all five tracks. King Abdulaziz University (1447): early childhood programme accepts all five tracks.

ARCH.usual_pattern: Architecture sits with the scientific colleges: Computer Science and Engineering, General or Health and Life track; scientific Achievement Test.
ARCH.examples:
King Saud University (1446): architecture and planning accepts the three scientific tracks only.
Qassim University (1447): architecture and planning requires a skills test.

DESIGN.usual_pattern: Design and fine arts sit with the humanities colleges: any track; an aptitude test or portfolio is common.
DESIGN.examples:
King Saud University (1446): fine arts accepts all five tracks.
Qassim University (1447): fine arts and design admitted on the 50/50 school-and-aptitude score.

MEDIA.examples: King Saud University (1446) and King Abdulaziz University (1447): humanities colleges accept all five tracks.

ARTS.examples: King Saud University (1446): languages, tourism and archaeology, and fine arts accept all five tracks.

SPORT.usual_pattern: Any track, plus the college's own admission test.
SPORT.examples:
King Saud University (1446): sports sciences and physical activity accepts all five tracks and requires its own admission test.
Qassim University (1447): sports sciences admitted on the 50/50 school-and-aptitude score.

APPLIED.usual_pattern: Military, police, aviation and technical colleges have their own entry rules, often including a scientific track, fitness and age limits.

Egypt.note: Thanaweya Amma sections (Sciences, Mathematics, Literary) and the new Baccalaureate tracks (Medicine and Life Sciences; Engineering and Computer Science; Business; Arts and Humanities). The official faculty mapping for Baccalaureate tracks was not published as of August 2026.

MED.thanaweya_amma_section: Sciences (علمي علوم): medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary medicine.
MED.baccalaureate_track_expected: Medicine and Life Sciences: biology and chemistry (advanced) in grade 12, maths or physics in grade 11. Expected to be the only track for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary medicine, physiotherapy and nursing (academic analysis, Apr 2026).
MED.international_certificates: IGCSE: 8 O-levels including biology, chemistry, physics, maths and English at C. American: 8 subjects including the same five, plus SAT, ACT or EST. IB: HL chemistry and biology.

PHARM.international_certificates: As for medicine. MSA University (pharmacy): IGCSE 8 subjects with English, maths, biology, chemistry, physics; IB: HL biology and chemistry; American: the same five plus a subject test including biology.

ALLIED.thanaweya_amma_section: Sciences: nursing, physiotherapy, applied health sciences.
ALLIED.international_certificates: As for medicine (physiotherapy is in the same group).

ENG.thanaweya_amma_section: Mathematics (علمي رياضة): engineering, petroleum and mining engineering, fine arts (architecture).
ENG.baccalaureate_track_expected: Engineering and Computer Science: maths and physics (advanced) in grade 12, chemistry or programming in grade 11. Expected to be the only track for engineering, urban planning, computers and information, AI and fine arts architecture (academic analysis, Apr 2026).
ENG.international_certificates: IGCSE: 9 subjects including English, maths, chemistry, physics and one AS or A-level maths. American: 9 subjects including advanced maths, maths, chemistry, physics and English (or 8 with a maths subject test). IB: HL maths and physics.

COMP.international_certificates: Listed under both the medicine and engineering groups in the guidelines: confirm with the university.

INFOSYS.thanaweya_amma_section: Mathematics (computers and information); some higher institutes of computer science also take the Literary section.
INFOSYS.baccalaureate_track_expected: Engineering and Computer Science, or Business.
INFOSYS.international_certificates: As for computing or business, by programme.

LIFESCI.thanaweya_amma_section: Faculty of Science: listed under Mathematics in the 2026 lists; biology departments usually take the Sciences section. Agriculture: Sciences and Mathematics.
LIFESCI.status: Partly sourced: confirm science faculty rules by section

PHYSMATH.thanaweya_amma_section: Mathematics: Faculty of Science. Statistics: commerce, economics and political science.

ECONFIN.thanaweya_amma_section: All three sections: commerce. Sciences and Literary: economics and political science.
ECONFIN.baccalaureate_track_expected: Business: economics (advanced) and maths in grade 12, accounting or business administration in grade 11. Expected: commerce and economics open to the Business track and to the scientific tracks (academic analysis, Apr 2026).
ECONFIN.international_certificates: IGCSE or American: 8 subjects including English, the rest from the Ministry list. IB: 6 subjects including English, 3 HL and 3 SL (MSA management sciences; Badya business).

BUSMGMT.thanaweya_amma_section: All three sections: commerce, tourism and hotels.

LAW.thanaweya_amma_section: All three sections: law. Law in English: Mathematics and Literary in the 2026 lists.

SOC.thanaweya_amma_section: Sciences and Literary: arts, economics and political science. Literary: social work.
SOC.baccalaureate_track_expected: Arts and Humanities: psychology in grade 11, geography (advanced) and statistics in grade 12. Expected: arts, social work, law, media, tourism and education open to all four tracks (academic analysis, Apr 2026).

EDU.thanaweya_amma_section: All three sections: education, specific education, early childhood.

ARCH.thanaweya_amma_section: Mathematics: engineering (architecture departments) and fine arts (architecture department).

DESIGN.thanaweya_amma_section: Mathematics: applied arts. Literary (and Sciences for some departments): fine arts. Interior design at private universities: scientific sections only.
DESIGN.baccalaureate_track_expected: Arts and Humanities, or Engineering for applied arts (not yet official).
DESIGN.international_certificates: MSA arts and design: interior design needs the science subjects (English, maths, biology or AS maths, chemistry, physics; IB HL biology and chemistry or HL maths and physics); fashion, graphic and media, cinema and theatre: English plus 7 subjects from the Ministry list.

ARTS.thanaweya_amma_section: Sciences and Literary: arts, languages (Alsun), archaeology, music education.
ARTS.baccalaureate_track_expected: Arts and Humanities (expected). Languages (Alsun) expected to need the second foreign language elective in grade 11 (academic analysis, Apr 2026).
ARTS.international_certificates: MSA languages: IGCSE or American 8 subjects including English and a second foreign language; IB 6 subjects including English and a second foreign language.

APPLIED.thanaweya_amma_section: Police Academy (2026): any Thanaweya Amma or Azhar certificate at 65% or above, Egyptian nationality, age and height limits, then aptitude, medical, fitness, psychological, language and IT tests. Military colleges: own rules.
